wikibiome-media-program.name: WikiBiome editorial media program
wikibiome-media-program.scope: Scientific references, subject or morphology, non-diagnostic limits, identifiers, accessibility, metadata, and publication disposition. Final integration authority remains with the WikiBiome control task.

scientificReferenceCheck.notes: PubChem confirms elemental identity, identifiers, and silvery metallic appearance.

subjectReview.notes: Pellets and irregular metallic specimens are presented as a non-diagnostic technical visualization.

accessibilityReview.notes: Alt text identifies material and field; caption separately qualifies purity and processing variation.

nickel|nickel-technical-specimen-v2.webp.notes: Existing reviewed asset re-audited. Its master is explicitly a preservation reconstruction from the reviewed WebP, not an original generation master.

scientificReferenceCheck.notes: NCBI and the type-strain paper support species identity and restrained oval, nonmotile morphology.

subjectReview.notes: An isolated oval cell is shown without flagella or spores; the caption limits surface-detail generalization.

accessibilityReview.notes: Alt text states visible form and surface detail; caption adds biological qualifications and illustration status.

scientificReferenceCheck.notes: NCBI confirms genus identity; the morphology study supports bifid, club-shaped, and species-variable rods.

subjectReview.notes: Representative Y/V and clubbed forms are shown with genus-level variability disclosed.

bifidobacterium|bifidobacterium-morpholo.notes: Existing reviewed asset re-audited; preservation-master reconstruction remains explicitly disclosed.

scientificReferenceCheck.notes: NCBI confirms species identity; the morphogenesis review supports budding yeast and pseudohyphal states.

alzheimers-disease|alzheimers-disease-pa.notes: Existing reviewed asset re-audited; preservation-master reconstruction remains explicitly disclosed.

scientificReferenceCheck.notes: MeSH and the ecological review support a community-level state rather than a single organism.

dysbiosis|dysbiosis-microbial-community-.notes: Existing reviewed asset re-audited; preservation-master reconstruction remains explicitly disclosed.

scientificReferenceCheck.notes: NCBI confirms species identity and supports bacillary morphology with peritrichous flagella.

subjectReview.notes: Three rounded bacilli bear peritrichous flagella and fine pili; appendage variation is disclosed.

accessibilityReview.notes: Alt text distinguishes body shape and appendages; caption adds variability and illustration status.

escherichia-coli|escherichia-coli-morpho.notes: Existing reviewed asset re-audited; preservation-master reconstruction remains explicitly disclosed.

helicobacter-pylori|helicobacter-pylori-.notes: Existing reviewed asset re-audited; preservation-master reconstruction remains explicitly disclosed.

scientificReferenceCheck.notes: NCBI and MeSH establish genus identity and Gram-negative diplococcal morphology.

acidaminococcus|acidaminococcus-morpholo.notes: Accepted in microorganisms batch 001 after visual and scientific review.

acinetobacter|acinetobacter-morphology-v.notes: Accepted in microorganisms batch 001 after visual and scientific review.

scientificReferenceCheck.notes: NCBI confirms species identity; the reviewed source supports short pleomorphic, nonmotile coccobacilli.

subjectReview.notes: Five coccobacilli include a pair and restrained capsular boundaries; no flagella or hospital symbolism.

accessibilityReview.notes: Alt text describes count, shape, pair, and halo; caption adds nonmotility and non-diagnostic limits.

acinetobacter-baumannii|acinetobacter-ba.notes: Accepted in microorganisms batch 001 after visual and scientific review.

scientificReferenceCheck.notes: NCBI confirms phylum rank; the review documents coccoid, rod-coccoid, fragmenting hyphal, and branched mycelial diversity.

subjectReview.notes: Four separated groups communicate phylum breadth without assigning one morphology or literal relative scale.

accessibilityReview.notes: Alt text enumerates visible groups; caption explains phylum diversity and illustrative scale.

actinobacteria|actinobacteria-microbial-.notes: Accepted in microorganisms batch 001 as a phylum-level microbial-community treatment.

scientificReferenceCheck.notes: NLM sources support nonmotile filamentous rods, branching forms, and possible clubbed ends.

subjectReview.notes: Revised draft v2 preserves segmented branching rods and clubbed ends while removing every appendage-like hair.

actinomyces|actinomyces-morphology-v1.we.notes: Approved only after control-tower rejection of the hair-bearing first draft and targeted image edit.

subjectReview.notes: Ordinary bacilli bear peritrichous flagella and fine pili; caption states AIEC is functionally defined and not morphologically diagnostic.

accessibilityReview.notes: Alt text identifies rods and appendages only; caption carries the essential pathotype limitation.

adherent-invasive-e-coli|adherent-invasi.notes: Accepted in microorganisms batch 001 with explicit pathotype limitation.

scientificReferenceCheck.notes: NCBI confirms the genus; original and emended descriptions support nonmotile, non-spore-forming coccobacillary-to-rod morphology.

subjectReview.notes: Control-tower visual review counted six cells spanning ovoid coccobacilli to rounded rods, with no appendages or spores.

accessibilityReview.notes: Alt text records six visible cells and the paired arrangement; caption separately states genus-level scope and non-micrograph status.

adlercreutzia|adlercreutzia-morphology-v.notes: Accepted by WikiBiome control-tower visual review in microorganisms batch 002.

scientificReferenceCheck.notes: NCBI confirms the genus; primary isolate characterization supports cocci in pairs, tetrads, and clusters.

subjectReview.notes: Control-tower visual review accepted the separated tetrad, pair, and irregular cluster with no chains, appendages, or spores.

accessibilityReview.notes: Alt text enumerates the three visible arrangements; caption supplies genus-level and non-diagnostic limits.

aerococcus|aerococcus-morphology-v1.webp.notes: Accepted by WikiBiome control-tower visual review in microorganisms batch 002.

scientificReferenceCheck.notes: NCBI confirms the genus; electron-microscopy studies support straight rods, one polar flagellum in motile mesophilic strains, and conditional lateral flagella.

subjectReview.notes: V1 was rejected for a lophotrichous-looking tuft. Control accepted v2 only: four rods, three with exactly one polar flagellum and one without a visible appendage.

accessibilityReview.notes: Alt text records four rods and the three single-polar appendages; caption qualifies species and growth-condition variation.

aeromonas|aeromonas-morphology-v1.webp.notes: Accepted by WikiBiome control-tower visual review only after the v1→revise→v2 chain.

scientificReferenceCheck.notes: NCBI confirms the genus. The 2016 record supports a motile Gram-negative rod-shaped strain; the original A. fetalis description is nonmotile; later A. aestuarii taxonomy supports motile members with one polar flagellum.

subjectReview.notes: Conditional acceptance followed a human recount: six rods are visible, not the five requested by the immutable prompt. Exactly two show one polar flagellum, representing genus-level variation rather than a universal state.

accessibilityReview.notes: Alt text, caption, description, manifest, and structured metadata consistently record six rods and explicitly avoid implying that every Alishewanella cell or strain is flagellated.

alishewanella|alishewanella-morphology-v.notes: Accepted after metadata/evidence correction. The asset remains explicitly a reconstruction, not a micrograph or diagnostic image.

revisionLinkage.auditCorrection: prompt requested five; output audit observed six

scientificReferenceCheck.notes: NCBI confirms the genus; electron-microscopy-backed descriptions support nonmotile, non-spore-forming ovoid-to-short-rod forms.

subjectReview.notes: Control-tower visual review accepted six ovoid-to-short-rod cells, including one loose pair, with no appendages or spores.

accessibilityReview.notes: Alt text records the six visible cells and shape range; caption separately qualifies genus-level variability and non-diagnostic use.

alistipes|alistipes-morphology-v1.webp.notes: Accepted by WikiBiome control-tower visual review in microorganisms batch 002.

scientificReferenceCheck.notes: NCBI confirms the genus; the original A. rava description supports nonmotile bacilli occurring singly or in short chains with substantial length variation.

subjectReview.notes: Conditional control acceptance was reconciled by human output audit: seven cells are visible, comprising a three-cell chain and four singles, not the six requested by the prompt.

accessibilityReview.notes: Alt text, manifest, and registry consistently state seven bacilli and the three-cell-chain arrangement; caption carries genus-level and non-diagnostic limits.

alloprevotella|alloprevotella-morphology.notes: Accepted after correcting every count-bearing output description from six to seven while preserving the original prompt record.

alloscardovia|alloscardovia-morphology-v.notes: Accepted after replacing the inaccurate “seven rods” assertion with audited grouping language while preserving the original prompt record.

accessibilityReview.notes: Alt text identifies the hypha, three conidia, and both septum directions; caption separately provides variability and non-diagnostic limits.

subjectReview.notes: Control accepted three separated coccal arrangements: one tetrad, one irregular clump, and one pair, with no chains, appendages, or spores.

accessibilityReview.notes: Alt text enumerates the visible arrangements; caption adds type-species context and non-diagnostic scope.

anaerococcus|anaerococcus-morphology-v1..notes: Accepted by WikiBiome control-tower visual review in microorganisms batch 003.

scientificReferenceCheck.notes: NCBI confirms the genus; the original A. caccae description supports Gram-variable, obligately anaerobic, asporogenous rods.

subjectReview.notes: Conditional control acceptance was reconciled by human output audit: seven cells are visible as three singles, one loose pair, and one attached two-cell arrangement, not the six requested by the prompt.

accessibilityReview.notes: Alt text, manifest, and registry consistently state seven rods and their arrangements; caption avoids an unsupported stain-color claim and supplies non-diagnostic scope.

anaerostipes|anaerostipes-morphology-v1..notes: Accepted after correcting every count-bearing output description from six to seven while preserving the original prompt record.

scientificReferenceCheck.notes: NCBI confirms NCBITaxon:244127 and genus rank; original and emended descriptions support anaerobic pleomorphic rods and occasional oval terminal spores.

subjectReview.notes: Control accepted seven thin bacilli, including one pair and exactly one terminal endospore, with no appendages or clinical narrative.

accessibilityReview.notes: Alt text records seven visible rods, the loose pair, and one terminal spore; caption supplies type-species and non-diagnostic qualifications.

anaerotruncus|anaerotruncus-morphology-v.notes: Accepted by WikiBiome control-tower visual review in microorganisms batch 004.

scientificReferenceCheck.notes: NCBI confirms the genus; CDC microscopy supports a smooth conidiophore, vesicle, biseriate supporting cells, conidial chains, and species-level variability.

subjectReview.notes: Control accepted one organized conidial head with its septate hypha, smooth stalk, vesicle, supporting layers, and short spherical chains legible, without environmental or host scenery.

accessibilityReview.notes: Alt text names the conidial-head structures in reading order; caption separately qualifies species variability and non-diagnostic use.

aspergillus|aspergillus-morphology-v1.we.notes: Accepted by WikiBiome control-tower visual review in microorganisms batch 004.

scientificReferenceCheck.notes: NCBI confirms current genus NCBITaxon:1380 and type species A. minutum NCBITaxon:1381; original and DSMZ records support elliptical-to-short-rod morphology.

subjectReview.notes: Control accepted the current-genus treatment showing nine cells; the image and caption explicitly exclude species now assigned to Lancefieldella or Fannyhessea.

accessibilityReview.notes: Alt text records nine visible cells and their single, pair, and chain arrangements; caption states the current-genus scope and excluded reclassified species.

atopobium|atopobium-morphology-v1.webp.notes: Accepted only for current-genus Atopobium. The separate atopobium-parvulum and atopobium-vaginae canonical routes remain on scientific-identity hold and have no assets.

scientificReferenceCheck.notes: NCBI and taxonomic work support the emended sensu-stricto genus; electron microscopy supports vegetative rods and dormant endospore structure.

subjectReview.notes: Control accepted five rods, two internal non-swelling oval spores, and one separate mature spore, without flagella, anthrax-specific chains, capsule, or disease narrative.

accessibilityReview.notes: Alt text identifies rod and spore counts; caption separately qualifies genus scope, variation, and non-diagnostic status.

bacillus|bacillus-morphology-v1.webp.notes: Accepted by WikiBiome control-tower visual review in microorganisms batch 004.

rejectedAssets.reason: Neither NCBI Taxonomy nor LPSN recognizes Akkermansia mucinicola, so no controlled taxonomic identifier or morphology description can support a publishable image.
rejectedAssets.requiredResolution: Correct or retire the canonical route, or supply an authoritative taxonomic description and controlled identifier. The route remains uncovered until the hold is removed through review.

rejectedAssets.reason: NCBI now treats Allisonella histaminiformans as the basionym of Dialister histaminiformans, while the canonical article instead names unsupported Allisonella hiatal and assigns an incompatible taxonomic identity. No publishable subject can be keyed to the route without correcting its scope.
rejectedAssets.requiredResolution: Correct the canonical article to the current Dialister histaminiformans identity, explicitly reframe Allisonella as a historical synonym, or retire the route. A controlled identifier and corrected scientific scope are required before media review can proceed.

rejectedAssets.reason: NCBI recognizes Lancefieldella parvula as the current name for NCBITaxon:1382 and lists Atopobium parvulum only as a homotypic synonym. Publishing new media under the superseded combination would misstate the current identity.
rejectedAssets.requiredResolution: Rename or redirect the canonical route to Lancefieldella parvula, or explicitly scope the article as a historical synonym page keyed to NCBITaxon:1382, before media review proceeds.

rejectedAssets.reason: NCBI recognizes Fannyhessea vaginae as the current name for NCBITaxon:82135 and lists Atopobium vaginae as its basionym. Publishing new media under the superseded combination would misstate the current identity.
rejectedAssets.requiredResolution: Rename or redirect the canonical route to Fannyhessea vaginae, or explicitly scope the article as a historical synonym page keyed to NCBITaxon:82135, before media review proceeds.

revisedAssets.reason: Fine hair-like projections could read as pili or flagella and conflicted with the nonmotile framing.
revisedAssets.outcome: Targeted edit removed every appendage-like hair while preserving segmented branching rods and clubbed ends.

revisedAssets.reason: The upper-right cell carried a lophotrichous-looking polar tuft rather than the restrained single-polar form selected for the canonical genus treatment.
revisedAssets.outcome: Targeted edit removed the extra strands and retained exactly one fine polar flagellum on that cell without changing the other rods. Control-tower visual review accepted v2, and only v2 was promoted.

notes: Drafts remain outside the public media registry and public/media-files.
Only assets with a matching approved review entry may enter the registry.
Scientific-identity holds remain uncovered, are skipped by generation batches, and must be resolved before any registry publication.
The eight baseline masters are preservation reconstructions from reviewed WebP derivatives, not original generation masters.
